paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, I hope today is another great day for you.

As to updates, we've had several emails from the Area Presidency over the past couple of days reminding all the Church leaders in the Philippines to not hold online sacrament or testimony meetings during the quarantine. While the First Presidency has authorized the sacrament ordinance at home by worthy priesthood holders, the actual meetings should not be recreated in an online format through Zoom or other video conferencing or audio conferencing platforms.

Instead, the Area Presidency has suggested a format of different types of online meetings that could be held, such as devotionals, Relief Society and Young Women meetings, and priesthood meetings. There's actually a suggested schedule for these meetings and each stake president should have already received it. So as missionaries, we also need to abide by the direction provided by the First Presidency and not do more than they have authorized in our Sunday activities.

Okay, as to the podcast, I've decided to take the next few days and do an in-depth book review of a very special little book called Drawing on the Powers of Heaven, which was written by a man by the name of Grant von Harrison. This little book has been a powerful force for good for many, many people including myself and Sister Hughes. When I was a missionary, it was actually a part of the missionary library that we studied regularly. The primary focus of the book is how to build and exercise faith. So let's get started.

Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles encouraged the members in his day to, quote, "learn how to pray boldly and efficaciously, not in word only, but in spirit and in power, so that we may pull upon ourselves the very powers of heaven," close quote.

The powers of heaven are very real and can dramatically influence the course of events in a person's life. What are the powers of heaven? Well, they include any influence or power from God, such as inspiration, revelation, gifts of the Spirit, power in the priesthood, and many other interventions that God can bring about in our behalf. They are virtually unlimited and certainly beyond our understanding to fully comprehend.

But even at your young ages, elders and sisters, you have already felt the powers of heaven at one time or another and perhaps many times. To realize, however, your full potential in your mortal life, you must learn to draw upon the powers of heaven regularly. No amount of skill or knowledge can make up for the absence of the powers of heaven active in your life.

With these powers, you can be very successful in mortality even with your mortal weaknesses because the powers of heaven are literally given to us to compensate for our mortal weaknesses. Just like with Moroni in Ether chapter 12, as you learn how to call upon and draw down the powers of heaven, your limitations—your mental, emotional, and physical capacities—become insignificant. The Lord promises you, just as he did Moroni, that if you come unto him in humility with sufficient faith, your weaknesses will become strengths. If you learn how to pull down the powers of heaven upon yourself, your talents and abilities will actually be magnified.

President Ezra Taft Benson said, quote, "Men and women who turn their lives over to God will discover that he can make a lot more out of their lives than they can. He will deepen their joys, expand their vision, quicken their minds, strengthen their muscles, lift their spirits, multiply their blessings, increase their opportunities, comfort their souls, raise up friends, and pour out peace. Whoever will lose his life in the service of God will find eternal life," close quote.

That is another promise that you can rely on as you gain confidence in your ability to draw upon the powers of heaven. The powers of heaven are governed by spiritual laws and they are accessed by obedience to those laws, just as all other blessings are accessed. If you have any question about this, you should review Doctrine and Covenants section 130 verses 20 and 21.

Understanding this principle is key. So it is through your own efforts that you actually qualify for the gifts and the blessings that are available to you through the powers of heaven. As Doctrine and Covenants 121:36 states clearly, quote, "the powers of heaven cannot be controlled nor handled only upon the principles of righteousness," close quote.

Once you realize that the principles of heaven and the powers of heaven, rather, are governed by law, you will hopefully become motivated to learn those laws whereby you can call down these powers. You obviously can't be obedient to laws and principles that you don't know about or understand. By the time we get through with this podcast or series of podcasts, you will have a pretty good overview of Grant Von Harrison's little book, Drawing on the Powers of Heaven.

And with that, you will hopefully gain an even better understanding of faith and especially the processes of faith that govern the powers of heaven. You will also understand better the role our thoughts play in the exercising of faith and how to cope with the trials of your faith, which we all have to experience in this mortal probation.

In the course of these podcasts, you will come to see that there is much more to the process of exercising faith than you had probably thought. Most members of the church have a very limited view of faith. Their understanding is usually based upon Hebrews 11 and Alma 32. And that is great as far as it goes. But a person's ability to draw upon the power of heaven is extremely limited unless he or she understands very specifically the process required to actually exercise faith.

The ability to state a vague definition of faith is not enough. Exercising faith sufficient to draw upon the powers of heaven involves a very specific process. You must understand the process very well and learn how to apply it in your daily pursuits in life. That is how you actually see the blessings of heaven being bestowed upon you, which is what God wants for all of his children.

So in conclusion, even though faith is a gift of God, we only obtain that gift by exercising our agency. I want to say that again to make sure you understand this point. A person increases and perfects his faith only through the exercise of agency.

As we go forward in faith, exercising our agency, sometimes minute by minute, we ultimately are able to understand the process of how faith is the lever by which we draw upon and call down upon ourselves the powers of heaven. These powers not only can magnify your talents and gifts and compensate for your weaknesses and challenges, but they can open up for your families blessings. They can open up ways for you to bless your family, even from a distance, such as you are at a distance from your family right now in the mission field.

It's so important that you begin to realize that faith transcends distance. The powers of heaven transcend distance. They transcend circumstances in the mortal world. And so that by drawing upon them, we place ourselves in a position to bring about righteousness and goodness and blessings in our lives and in the lives of those we have responsibility to serve and care for.

I testify to you that this is true, and I am happy to share these thoughts with you, which don't come entirely from me for sure, but I have proven them to be true in my own life. Afternoon, elders and sisters, make the rest of your day great through the exercise of your agency. We love you. We pray for your success and happiness, and look forward to talking with you tomorrow.
